sites.name: Hadimba Devi Temple
sites.overview: Bahadur Singh commissioned the surviving shrine in 1553. The sanctuary encloses a natural rock associated with local worship; epic traditions are not treated as construction dates.

sites.name: Masrur Rock-cut Temples
sites.overview: The monolithic complex belongs to the early medieval period. Earthquake damage and unfinished portions remain part of its architectural history; a securely identified royal commissioner is not recorded here.

sites.name: Tabo Monastery
sites.overview: The monastery was founded in 996 under western Tibetan royal patronage. Its painted interiors and later buildings represent several phases, rather than one unchanged tenth-century structure.

sites.name: Alchi Monastery
sites.overview: The Alchi religious complex preserves early western Himalayan Buddhist art. The dates refer to its historic temple phases; attribution to a single founder or dynasty remains qualified.

sites.name: Thiksey Monastery
sites.overview: The Gelug monastery developed on a hill near Leh. Its foundation and the many later structures should be read as different phases; the record does not assign the whole complex to one royal patron.

sites.name: Kedarnath Temple
sites.overview: Kedarnath is a major Himalayan pilgrimage shrine. Traditions about its sacred origins are distinguished from the uncertain dating of the surviving stone building.

sites.name: Badrinath Temple
sites.overview: The Vishnu shrine forms part of the Himalayan Char Dham pilgrimage. Its present appearance incorporates rebuilding and repairs, so this record leaves an exact original construction year unknown.

sites.name: Katarmal Sun Temple
sites.overview: ASI distinguishes evidence of earlier brick and wooden members from the surviving stone temple, which it places in the twelfth–thirteenth centuries. Popular early foundation dates are not applied to every surviving component.

sites.name: Sheikh Chilli's Tomb
sites.overview: The funerary ensemble includes two tombs, a madrasa and gardens. Its seventeenth-century Mughal context is recorded separately from uncertain biographical identifications of the saint.

sites.name: Chandigarh Capitol Complex
sites.overview: Le Corbusier and collaborators designed the civic ensemble after Indian independence. It is included as a documented modern heritage exception, not as architecture of an ancient empire.

sites.name: Gobindgarh Fort
sites.overview: The fort passed from the Bhangi Misl to Maharaja Ranjit Singh and later British control. Sikh-period strengthening is recorded as an addition, not as the first construction of every wall.

sites.name: Pari Mahal
sites.overview: Prince Dara Shukoh developed the terraced garden around 1650 during Shah Jahan's reign. Its documented Mughal patronage does not establish the date of every surviving repair.

sites.name: Avantiswami Temple
sites.overview: Avantivarman of the Utpala dynasty commissioned the ninth-century shrine. The record concentrates on the Avantiswami precinct rather than treating nearby temples as one building.

sites.name: Kamakhya Temple
sites.overview: The shrine has earlier origins and repeated rebuilding. Koch ruler Naranarayan is associated with the major sixteenth-century reconstruction; later additions form part of its layered history.

sites.name: Rang Ghar
sites.overview: The Ahom royal pavilion served as a viewing place for games and gatherings near the former Rangpur capital. Its masonry phase belongs to the eighteenth century.

sites.name: Charaideo Moidams
sites.overview: The Ahom royal necropolis developed over centuries. UNESCO inscribed the property in 2024; that recognition date is separate from the construction and use of the burial mounds.

sites.name: Nartiang Durga Temple
sites.overview: The Durga shrine is associated with Jaintia religious history. Sources describe centuries of worship, but a precise date for the photographed structure is not established here.

sites.name: Kangla Fort
sites.overview: Kangla was the seat of Manipuri rulers until 1891. The palace precinct contains remains and renewed sacred structures; its traditional foundation chronology is not used as the date of every building.

sites.name: Ujjayanta Palace
sites.overview: Maharaja Radha Kishore Manikya commissioned the palace in 1899–1901. It later accommodated the state legislature and now serves as a museum.

sites.name: Neermahal
sites.overview: Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya built the lake palace as a summer residence during 1930–1938. Its princely patronage is distinct from an attribution to Mughal imperial rule.

sites.name: Kachari Rajbari Ruins
sites.overview: The site is associated with the Dimasa Kachari kingdom. Official and secondary summaries differ on dates, and the original purpose of the sculpted pillars is uncertain.

sites.name: Pemayangtse Monastery
sites.overview: Founded as an early religious establishment, the monastery was enlarged under Sikkim's Chogyal rulers. Sources distinguish its seventeenth-century beginnings from eighteenth-century expansion.

sites.name: Rabdentse Palace Ruins
sites.overview: Rabdentse served as a capital of the Namgyal kingdom of Sikkim. The date range describes the capital's period of use, not a continuous construction campaign.

sites.name: Malinithan Temple Ruins
sites.overview: The archaeological site preserves a medieval temple and sculptural remains. Arunachal Tourism associates the phase with Chutiya rulers; this is a qualified historical attribution.

sites.name: Sibuta Lung
sites.overview: The memorial is associated with the Palian chief Sibuta at Tachhip. Accounts of its erection belong partly to oral tradition, and no precise construction year is imposed here. Map position is an approximate Sibutalung locality reference, not a surveyed position of the stone.

sites.name: Bhoramdeo Temple
sites.overview: The main stone Shiva shrine forms part of a group that also includes earlier and later monuments. Its medieval architecture is associated with the region's Nagavanshi rulers.

sites.name: Lakshmana Temple, Sirpur
sites.overview: Queen Vasata commissioned the Vishnu shrine in memory of Harshagupta in the Panduvamshi period. It belongs to Sirpur's wider, multi-religious archaeological landscape.

sites.name: Maluti Temples
sites.overview: The village's patron families sponsored successive temples rather than one unified royal palace. Sources associate the temple-building tradition with the Baj Basanta family.

sites.name: Jagannath Temple, Ranchi
sites.overview: The original hilltop shrine was founded in the seventeenth century under local Nagvanshi patronage. Parts of the present building reflect reconstruction after a twentieth-century collapse.

sites.name: Tomb of Sher Shah Suri
sites.overview: Sher Shah Suri's mausoleum was completed in 1545 during the Sur dynasty. Its commemorative function and completion are distinguished from the emperor's earlier political career.

sites.name: Hazarduari Palace
sites.overview: Nawab Humayun Jah commissioned the palace, designed by Duncan MacLeod. Its European architectural vocabulary does not erase the agency of its Nawabi patron.

sites.name: Unakoti Rock-cut Reliefs
sites.overview: The reliefs predate Manikya rule. UNESCO's tentative-list account dates them stylistically to the eighth–ninth centuries; a specific royal patron is not established.

sites.name: Mukteshwar Temple
sites.overview: The tenth-century Shiva shrine occupies an important place in the development of Odisha temple architecture. A dynastic-period association is not treated as proof of a named commissioner.

sites.name: Bhojeshwar Temple
sites.overview: The unfinished Shiva temple is associated with Paramara ruler Bhoja. Nearby quarry marks and architectural drawings are important evidence of its construction process.

sites.name: Datia Palace
sites.overview: Bir Singh Deo commissioned the palace. Official accounts give differing early-seventeenth-century dates, retained here as an uncertainty range rather than one exact construction year.

sites.name: Dashavatara Temple, Deogarh
sites.overview: The Vishnu shrine belongs to the Gupta-period architectural tradition. Its surviving reliefs and platform are early evidence of a developed structural temple plan.

sites.name: Adalaj Stepwell
sites.overview: Queen Rudabai's patronage is associated with the late-fifteenth-century stepwell. The monument belongs to a regional setting shaped by both local rulers and the Gujarat Sultanate.

sites.name: Lothal Archaeological Site
sites.overview: Lothal formed part of the Indus civilisation's settlement and trade network. The function of the large basin is discussed in archaeological interpretation; it is not presented here as an undisputed dock.

sites.name: Raigad Fort
sites.overview: Shivaji adapted the earlier hill fort as a Maratha capital and held his coronation there in 1674. Its history includes earlier occupation and later military events.

sites.name: Daulatabad Fort
sites.overview: The Yadava stronghold became the Delhi Sultanate's capital during Muhammad bin Tughluq's fourteenth-century transfer. Later Deccan rulers adapted the extensive defences.

sites.name: Sindhudurg Fort
sites.overview: Shivaji commissioned the island fort in the seventeenth century as part of Maratha coastal defence. The fort forms part of the Maratha Military Landscapes property inscribed in 2025.

sites.name: Gingee Fort
sites.overview: Gingee passed through Nayaka, Maratha, Mughal and other phases. It is not attributed wholesale to one emperor; Maratha adaptation is one documented layer.

sites.name: Bekal Fort
sites.overview: Kerala Tourism associates the fort's principal construction with Shivappa Nayaka of Ikkeri. Later control by Mysore belongs to a separate historical phase.

sites.name: Undavalli Caves
sites.overview: The caves preserve early medieval religious and architectural phases. Accounts differ on chronology and patronage, so the range remains broad and dynastic connections qualified.

sites.name: Thousand Pillar Temple
sites.overview: Rudra Deva commissioned the twelfth-century Kakatiya shrine. Its familiar name is not used as an independently verified count of every surviving pillar.

sites.name: Se Cathedral
sites.overview: The cathedral developed under Portuguese rule in Goa. Construction, consecration and later alterations are separate stages rather than a single date.

sites.name: Junagarh Fort
sites.overview: Raja Rai Singh's fort became the core of a palace ensemble enlarged by later Bikaner rulers. The dates describe the initial fort phase, not every decorated room.

sites.name: Gagron Fort
sites.overview: The fort changed hands among regional Rajput rulers and later powers. Its inclusion in the Hill Forts of Rajasthan property recognizes the landscape-based defensive ensemble.

sites.name: Diu Fort
sites.state: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu
sites.overview: The Portuguese developed the fort following an agreement with Gujarat's Sultan Bahadur Shah. Subsequent strengthening belongs to the wider sixteenth-century military history of Diu.

sites.name: Basilica of the Sacred Heart of Jesus
sites.overview: The Catholic church developed in the early twentieth century in French-administered Pondicherry. Its religious patronage is distinguished from a claim that the French state commissioned the building.
